papers.summary: Abstract Well placement design for underground hydrogen storage (UHS) faces the challenge of balancing hydrogen recovery, costs, and operational constraints. The objective is long-term net present value (NPV), which is normalized as total reward. papers.summary: We present a recurrent self-play reinforcement learning framework for autonomous beyond-visual-range (BVR) air combat under partial observability. The environment is formulated as a decision-level BVR missile-duel simulator that combines 3-DoF aircraft kinematics, field-of-view radar observation, track-quality decay, flight-envelope action masking, and an energy-aware missile model with boost, coast, drag, and proportional-navigation guidance. papers.title: Virtue by Observation: Social Reinforcement Learning for Intrinsically Ethical Agents
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning is increasingly deployed in settings with ethical stakes, yet rule-based and scalar-reward alignment approaches remain brittle and prone to proxy gaming. I argue that two of their most persistent failures, hallucination and moral drift, share a single structural cause, which I term \textit{feedback collapse}: the compression of plural human values into a static scalar reward by a fixed evaluation model. My research develops a virtue-centric alternative, Social Reinforcement Learning, in which evaluative authority is distributed across a dynamic population of peer agents.
